HOW TO READ THE PLAN

01 / Capacity is earned

Only safely routable capacity counts. A requested replica does not contribute while it starts or warms up.

02 / Delay creates a deficit

When demand crosses capacity before new workers arrive, the gap becomes work that must be deferred or rejected.

03 / Safety is a gate

Low utilization alone cannot authorize termination. Active work, unresolved effects, and sessions must be reconciled.

Model assumptions & calculation notes

This is a planning calculator, not a live autoscaler. It assumes homogeneous workers, linear nonnegative demand growth, constant existing capacity, and stepwise arrival of added capacity. Readiness delay should be a measured end-to-end quantile, not the mean boot time. The extra margin advances the trigger and extends the demand forecast; the deficit integrates only to the entered arrival delay.

Safe capacity = tested RPS × operating factor. Effective capacity = replicas × safe capacity × readiness contribution. Replica demand = ceil((current demand + growth × (delay + margin)) / safe capacity). Dependency throughput caps admission but cannot be solved by adding application workers.

Bridge deficit = ∫ max(0, demand + growth × time − admitted capacity) dt. Queue room is bounded by count and estimated wait budget. This fluid approximation does not guarantee per-request latency, memory safety, or deadlines. Defer work only when the operation contract allows it.

Failure-domain capacity uses (Regions − Region losses) × (AZs per Region − AZ losses per surviving Region) × safe RPS per AZ. Capacity arithmetic does not establish quorum, availability, RTO/RPO or consistency. Component latency allocations are budgets; adding independently measured p95 values does not yield an end-to-end p95. Concurrency uses the entered latency as a planning allowance, not a proven mean.
